title: I2C and SPI Protocols
subtitle: Two-wire vs four-wire protocols for sensors and displays

content.text: I2C uses just two wires (SDA data, SCL clock) and supports multiple devices via 7-bit addresses.
SPI is faster than I2C. It uses four wires: MOSI, MISO, SCK, and SS (chip select). Used for displays and SD cards.

questions.question: How many wires does I2C use?
questions.explanation: I2C uses two wires: SDA (data) and SCL (clock). Both are shared among all devices on the bus.

faq.q: When should I choose SPI over I2C?
faq.a: Use SPI when you need high speed (SD cards, displays). Use I2C when you need fewer wires and many devices. I2C is simpler to wire but slower.
